ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in triangle \(ABC\), \(AB=10\text{cm}\), \(AC=6\text{cm}\), \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\), and \(E\) is a point on side \(AB\). If the perimeter of triangle \(BDE\) is equal to the perimeter of quadrilateral \(ACDE\), find the length of segment \(AE\).
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the diagram, we have:\\
The perimeter of triangle $BDE = BE + BD + DE$, the perimeter of quadrilateral $ACDE = AE + AC + DC + DE$,\\
And since the perimeter of triangle $BDE$ equals the perimeter of quadrilateral $ACDE$, and $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$,\\
Therefore, $BD = DC$, $BE + BD + DE = AE + AC + DC + DE$,\\
Therefore, $BE = AE + AC$,\\
And since $AB= 10\text{cm}$, $AC = 6\text{cm}$, $BE = AB - AE$,\\
Therefore, $AE + AC = AB - AE$,\\
Therefore, $10 - AE = AE + 6$,\\
Therefore, $AE = \boxed{2\text{cm}}$.

The perimeter of triangle \(BDE\) is \(BE+BD+DE\), and the perimeter of quadrilateral \(ACDE\) is \(AE+AC+DC+DE\). Since these perimeters are equal and \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\), we have \(BD=DC\), so
\[BE+BD+DE=AE+AC+DC+DE\]
which gives
\[BE=AE+AC.\]
Also, since \(AB=10\text{ cm}\) and \(E\) lies on \(AB\), we have \(BE=AB-AE=10-AE\). With \(AC=6\text{ cm}\),
\[10-AE=AE+6.\]
Thus,
\[AE=2\text{ cm}.\]
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in triangle \(ABC\), \(AB=10\text{ cm}\), \(AC=6\text{ cm}\), \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\), and \(E\) is a point on side \(AB\). If the perimeter of triangle \(BDE\) is equal to the perimeter of quadrilateral \(ACDE\), find the length of segment \(AE\).
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Given the diagram, we have: The perimeter of triangle \(BDE\) is \(BE+BD+DE\), and the perimeter of quadrilateral \(ACDE\) is \(AE+AC+DC+DE\). Since these perimeters are equal and \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\), we have \(BD=DC\), so \[BE+BD+DE=AE+AC+DC+DE\] which gives \[BE=AE+AC.\] Also, since \(AB=10\text{ cm}\) and \(E\) lies on \(AB\), we have \(BE=AB-AE=10-AE\). With \(AC=6\text{ cm}\), \[10-AE=AE+6.\] Thus, \[AE=2\text{ cm}.\]
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, A is at the upper right; E is located on side AB, D is located on side BC, and segment DE is drawn. Therefore triangle BDE and quadrilateral ACDE share segment DE, and D divides BC into two segments BD and DC.

Reasoning: Given AB=10 cm, AC=6 cm, D is the midpoint of BC, so BD=DC. The perimeter of triangle BDE is BE+BD+DE, and the perimeter of quadrilateral ACDE is AE+AC+DC+DE. The two perimeters are equal, so BE+BD+DE=AE+AC+DC+DE. Because BD=DC, and DE appears on both sides, they can be canceled, obtaining BE=AE+AC. Also because E is on AB, AB=AE+BE, namely BE=10-AE. Substituting AC=6, obtain 10-AE=AE+6. Solving obtains 4=2AE, so AE=2 cm.
